notice: receipt.json is byte-frozen because the reviewer read and hashed it. Its claims are corrected here, and the remediation is in commit 36ebdfb9, which post-dates the reviewed tree.

corrections.what_it_said: that a second principal with equal roles and equal grants sees zero hits, therefore no cross-principal construction can vary the permission leg alone.
corrections.what_is_true: False. With a fresh CURRENT snapshot and nothing else varied (same project, same ProjectState revision 5=5, same manifest) a granted second principal gets hits=1 and the key moves. My zero hits were stale state inherited from the RefreshLocalSnapshots that ran earlier in the same test, so the row was describing my own sequencing, not the product.
corrections.remediation: The permission leg is now tested before anything mutates the snapshot, with the state revision pinned on both sides, and paired with a return-to-owner control. Two rows replace the false one: W0902-KEY-CHANGES-WHEN-THE-ACTING-PRINCIPAL-CHANGES and W0902-KEY-RESTORES-WHEN-THE-ORIGINAL-PRINCIPAL-RESUMES. Verified on my own tree: both pass, so the reviewer's disproof is reproduced rather than accepted on trust.
corrections.how_i_missed_it: I wrote the isolation attempt second in the test order because it read as a continuation of the key-movement story. The row asserted a reason ('visibility is bound to more than the grant set') that I had never tested in isolation - I had only ever observed it after a mutation. That is the same class as the compound-flip error: a plausible cause narrated over an unmeasured state.

corrections.receipt_field: assertion W0902-KEY-CHANGES-WHEN-SEALED-CONTENT-CHANGES detail 'varied: source bytes only'; actions_map claim that each runtime-varied leg was tested on its own
corrections.what_is_true: One RefreshLocalSnapshots moved the sealed content hash, that artifact's revision, its manifest membership and the ProjectState revision (5 -> 7) together. The invalidation is genuine; the attribution to a single source operand is not.
corrections.remediation: Renamed to W0902-KEY-CHANGES-WHEN-A-SEALED-ARTIFACT-IDENTITY-MOVES, and the row now lists the four things that moved and says the row proves the key follows the sealed identity, not the bytes alone.

corrections.what_is_true: The stated reason - a bundle needs a task, a task needs the accepted-requirement chain, a bare fixture requirement answers POST /tasks with 400 - describes only my fixture path. A green pre-existing test in the same package already exercises bundle creation. The real gap is that this handler's -run filter (^TestW0902) does not select it.
corrections.why_this_matters_more_than_the_wording: Calling an existing, passing guard 'unreachable' understates coverage in one direction and, if repeated in reverse, would overstate it in the other. Both are the same failure: concluding about a guard from my construction instead of from the tree.

corrections.receipt_field: mutation_matrix_note: 'The driver refuses, before executing, any replacement that removes more than one operand of a compound condition'
corrections.what_is_true: It only counted Go's && and ||. On Python conditions it counted zero operands, so it could never fire - and my own M12 replaced a two-operand Python condition with `if False:`, a whole-compound collapse, which executed and was reported as a survival. The reviewer's V06 would not have been refused either.
corrections.what_still_holds: The six 'caught' rows are genuinely caught and were reproduced independently. The overstatement is about the guard, not about those results.
corrections.remediation: operand_count now matches and/or on word boundaries as well as && and ||, strings are masked first, and an anchor-shrinking replacement is refused. The pair the matrix could not settle - both toolchain legs blinded at once - was run by the reviewer and CAUGHT, so W0902-TOOLCHAIN-REFUSES-A-REAL-BUT-WRONG-BINARY is a live guard; that result lives in the reviewer's own artifact, which is registered as evidence, rather than being claimed as mine.
corrections.recurrence: This is the third time on this line that a guard written after a rejection has itself been the weak link: the rule was stated correctly, the enforcement mechanism quietly did not apply to the case it was meant to catch, and only an outside run found it. Counting operators in one language out of two is enough to make the whole promise void, and nothing in my own pass would ever notice.

corrections.detail: The index row asserts only that backend_revision is non-empty; it never asserts fts5-v1 and stays green when the bounded-scan path serves the hit, so it cannot detect its own premise. And while the summary record does carry both kinds - the field addition is real and asserted - the receipt framed it as the CLI/Desktop projection: no HTTP route exposes EvidenceSupportSummary, its only non-test reader is the ADOPT gate, and the web client renders source_kind from the Evidence row itself. So action 3's 'same projection' half is not delivered by this change; the field is delivered, the projection is not.
corrections.disposition: Recorded, not fixed. Fixing the framing to 'shared summary used by the gate' is done in the renamed not_covered entry; making it an actual client projection needs a route, and the card that owns HTTP projection wiring is not W09-02.
